security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel IOMMU driver issues non-leaf PTE invalidation or address-range invalidation commands without first checking the IOMMU capabilities register for support of these extensions, or assumes all IOMMUs support fine-grained invalidation and skips full TLB flushes. This is most likely on RISC-V server SoCs where multiple IOMMUs may govern different PCIe hierarchies and may have heterogeneous capability sets, or where a non-PCIe IOMMU lacks extensions present on the PCIe-attached IOMMU.
affected_entities: IOMMU DDT/PCT entries with stale non-leaf TLB entries
security_spec.summary: Without capability checks for Non-Leaf PTE Invalidation (IOM_330) and Address Range Invalidation (IOM_340), stale IOMMU TLB entries can survive partial invalidation — a DMA device continues accessing memory through freed/reassigned page table entries, bypassing FreeBSD's pmap-driven memory protection for device contexts.

findings.finding: smmu_invalidate_all_sid() unconditionally issues CMD_CFGI_STE_RANGE (a range-based STE invalidation command) without first checking the SMMU_FEATURE_RANGE_INV capability flag. The capability is detected from IDR3_RIL at line 1470-1471 and stored in sc->features, but the guard is never consulted before emitting the command. On SMMUv3 implementations where IDR3.RIL=0, issuing CMD_CFGI_STE_RANGE results in CERROR_ILL (Illegal Command), which halts command queue processing and breaks all subsequent IOMMU invalidation. On RISC-V server SoCs with heterogeneous SMMU instances, some may lack range invalidation support even when others have it, making the unconditional use unsafe.

smmu_tlbi_va() unconditionally sets cmd.tlbi.leaf = true with the comment 'We change only L3'. The SMMUv3 architecture defines IDR3.BBML (bit 11) to indicate whether the TLB invalidation leaf parameter is supported. IDR3.BBML is not defined in smmureg.h and is never checked anywhere in the driver. On implementations where BBML=0 (leaf not supported), setting TLBI_1_LEAF in a CMD_TLBI_NH_VA produces architecturally UNPREDICTABLE behavior, potentially causing incomplete TLB invalidation and stale translation entries.

dmar_qi_invalidate_emit() unconditionally sets both DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_DW (Drain Writes) and DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_DR (Drain Reads) in every page-selective IOTLB invalidation descriptor on the QI path. These operations require DMAR_CAP_DWD (bit 54) and DMAR_CAP_DRD (bit 55) capability bits respectively. While the driver prints these capability bits during initialization (intel_drv.c:343), it never checks them before emitting DW/DR in the QI path. The non-QI register-based path (intel_idpgtbl.c:773) correctly checks DMAR_CAP_PSI before issuing page-selective invalidation and falls back to domain-selective invalidation when PSI is absent. The QI path has no such fallback. On hardware without drain read/write support, these bits are reserved and may cause command errors or be ignored, leading to incomplete invalidation and potential DMA to stale mappings.
findings.snippet:
dmar_qi_emit(unit, DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_INV |
    DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_PAGE | DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_DW |
    DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_DR |
    DMAR_IQ_DESCR_IOTLB_DID(domain->domain),
    base | am);

findings.finding: The AMD IOMMU kernel driver never issues INVALIDATE_IOTLB_PAGES commands (opcode 0x04, defined in amd_reg.h:666) to invalidate device IOTLBs. The qi_invalidate_emit function only issues INVALIDATE_IOMMU_PAGES (IOMMU TLB invalidation, not device IOTLB). PCIM_AMDIOMMU_CAP_IOTLB (pcireg.h:1148), which indicates hardware device-IOTLB support, is never referenced anywhere in the kernel IOMMU driver (amd_cmd.c, amd_drv.c, amd_ctx.c). Without device IOTLB invalidation, devices with ATS (Address Translation Services) retain stale cached translations after the IOMMU page tables are modified. This allows a device to continue DMA to memory pages that the OS has unmapped or reassigned — a direct privilege escalation path via stale ATS translations. Notably, the bhyve VMM AMD backend (amdvi_hw.c) does correctly check and handle device IOTLB invalidation, but the bare-metal kernel mapping path does not.

amdiommu_qi_invalidate_emit() unconditionally sets c.pde = 1 in every INVALIDATE_IOMMU_PAGES command, requesting non-leaf (intermediate page table) entry invalidation. The comment 'XXXKIB handle superpages' confirms this is known-incomplete. The code also sets isize = IOMMU_PAGE_SIZE and iterates page-by-page, which contradicts the non-leaf invalidation intent. The behavior of setting pde=1 without checking any hardware capability for non-leaf invalidation support, combined with the page-by-page loop, may cause incomplete or incorrect TLB invalidation on AMD IOMMU implementations that handle non-leaf invalidation differently.
